artifacts.name: BirthClinicSystem
artifacts.title: Birth clinic issuing system
artifacts.description:
The hospital system abroad that issues a DVC per dose with the HCERT library: the HCERT issuing system (smart-trust-tools) of a trust network participant (XXR).

**Persona**: Software that calls the library once per dose and never holds the private key; signs only with a DSC its country's CSCA issued and has already shared with the GDHCN.

**Also known as**: Issuer of the birth-dose DVCs (SMART Trust Issuer)

**Played in the journeys by**: Chiang Rai Provincial Hospital system, Thailand (Country A, XXR) (fictional).

artifacts.name: ChwApp

artifacts.description:

**Also known as**: Triage reader (SMART Trust Receiver, read-unverified)

artifacts.name: HomeClinicEhr
artifacts.title: Home clinic EHR
artifacts.description:
The clinic's OHS-based record system: verifies DVCs against the GDHCN trust list, imports them as FHIR Immunization resources and evaluates the national schedule (J3).

**Persona**: Holds the DID trust list from its last refresh, about weekly for a clinic without its own connection, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office; loading it is a precondition of a visit, and it verifies offline at the point of care.

**Also known as**: Verifier at the home clinic (SMART Trust Receiver)

**Played in the journeys by**: Vientiane District Health Center EHR (Country B) (fictional).

artifacts.name: NationalPortal

**Played in the journeys by**: Lao PDR national health portal and gateway (Country B, XXH) (fictional).

artifacts.name: PocReceiver
artifacts.title: Point-of-care receiver
artifacts.description:
The clinic system abroad that scans a VHL, verifies it, fetches the manifest (ITI-YY5) and decrypts the documents (J4.1): the VHL Receiver.

**Played in the journeys by**: Chiang Rai primary care clinic viewer, Thailand (J4.1) (fictional).

artifacts.name: TrustDemoLaoDvcVerification
artifacts.title: Lao PDR: foreign DVC verified against the GDHCN trust list
artifacts.description:
How it is used: J3a. The district EHR verifies each Thai DVC offline against its cached copy of the GDHCN trust list, then imports the dose. This record says so.

Why: a verified dose replaces a reported one, so the record must show who verified what, against which policy, and which reported doses it removes. Anyone who later doubts a dose can follow this record back to the signed certificate and the issuing country's key.

artifacts.name: TrustDemoLaoImmunization
artifacts.title: Lao PDR: dose on the national schedule
artifacts.description:
How it is used: J3 and after. These are the Thai birth doses once the district clinic has verified them, and every dose given in Lao PDR.

Why: the Lao schedule engine works on Lao EPI codes, so each dose must carry one. A dose that came from abroad keeps the issuer's product code beside the Lao one, added through the ConceptMap and confirmed by the nurse. Nothing the other country said is overwritten. A verified foreign dose is recorded from its primary source, the signing hospital, and its Provenance says how it was verified.

artifacts.name: TrustDemoLaoPatient
artifacts.title: Lao PDR: child registered by the community health worker
artifacts.description:
How it is used: J2 onwards. Vilay registers Somsack on a home visit, and the same patient carries every Lao record that follows: the verified Thai doses, the Lao doses and the summary shared in J4.

Why: a child born abroad is not in the Lao civil registry yet. A temporary id lets the CHW, the district clinic and the national portal all refer to the same child until civil registration catches up. The parents are recorded as contacts, because they hold the paper cards and later the family's VHLs.

artifacts.description:
How it is used: J2a. These are the CHW's answers on the newborn registration form, which the app renders with Structured Data Capture and saves with no signal.

artifacts.name: TrustDemoLaoReportedImmunization
artifacts.title: Lao PDR: foreign dose as reported (not yet verified)
artifacts.description:
How it is used: J2b. The CHW app reads each Thai paper DVC offline without checking its signature, and saves the dose like this.

Why: a CHW phone may have no trust list and no signal, but the doses should not be lost. Recording them with primarySource false and the family as the information source keeps them visibly "reported, not verified". The schedule will not count them until a clinic verifies them (J3). Only the issuer's product code is present, because mapping to the Lao schedule is a clinical step for later.

artifacts.name: TrustDemoLaoVhlAccess
artifacts.title: Lao PDR: every VHL access logged at home
artifacts.description:
How it is used: J4.1. The Lao national gateway records each attempt by a clinic abroad to fetch a family member's VHL manifest, the refused ones included.

Why: the family shares a link, not a copy, and the data stays in Lao PDR. Logging every access at home, following IHE Basic Audit Log Patterns, is what lets the family and the ministry see who looked, from where and when. A wrong passcode is logged too.

artifacts.name: TrustDemoThImmunization
artifacts.title: Thailand: dose given at the birth hospital (DVC source)
artifacts.description:
How it is used: J1. Each birth dose (Hep B, BCG) that Dr Anan gives is recorded here first. The hospital then packs it into a Digital Vaccination Certificate (HCERT, signed with XXR's key) and prints it as a QR card.

Why: the DVC can only carry what this record holds. The vaccine product, date, lot, dose number and the administering organization are exactly the fields the HCERT certificate needs. They are required here so every printed card is complete. The product is coded from the WHO PreQual-style product list, because that is the code Lao PDR will later map to its own schedule (J3).

artifacts.name: TrustDemoThPatient
artifacts.title: Thailand: newborn at the birth hospital
artifacts.description:
How it is used: J1. Chiang Rai Provincial Hospital registers Somsack under its own hospital number on the day he is born.

Why: a baby born to Lao parents in Thailand has no Thai citizen id, so the hospital number is the only identifier the hospital can put behind the dose records it signs. The DVCs it prints carry the name and date of birth, not this number. The family's home country therefore cannot rely on any Thai identifier, and links the doses to its own patient (see the Lao patient profile).

artifacts.name: TrustDemoThVhlReceipt
artifacts.title: Thailand: record of a summary read through a VHL
artifacts.description:
How it is used: J4.1. The Chiang Rai clinic viewer keeps this record when it opens Somsack's patient summary through the Verifiable Health Link that his father shows.

Why: the Thai clinic views the Lao record and does not copy it into a Thai registry. So the clinic keeps a note of what it saw, where it came from, and how it was verified: the VHL's signature against Lao PDR's key on the GDHCN trust list, the manifest fetch, and the passcode. The Lao side keeps its own log of the same access (the Lao audit profile).
